name: Hagia Sophia inaugurated
summary: Justinian I inaugurates the rebuilt Hagia Sophia on 27 December 537 after a five-year construction supervised by Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus. The 31-metre central dome on pendentives is the largest enclosed interior space in the world for nearly a thousand years.

_quarry.structural_significance: Canonical building of Byzantine architecture and a structural achievement that shapes domed-mosque traditions after 1453; the visual centre of imperial Orthodoxy for nine centuries.
